battery.label: Battery
battery.tip: Never put batteries in the wet or dry bin. Keep them separate and hand them over at a battery / e-waste collection point.

biological.label: Food / organic waste
biological.tip: Kitchen scraps, peels and leftovers. Compost at home if you can, otherwise give it to the wet-waste collection.

brown-glass.label: Brown glass
brown-glass.tip: Empty and rinse it. Wrap broken pieces in paper and label them so handlers are not hurt.

cardboard.label: Cardboard
cardboard.tip: Flatten it and keep it dry. Wet or greasy cardboard cannot be recycled well.

clothes.label: Clothes / textiles
clothes.tip: If still wearable, donate or reuse it. Otherwise give it to the dry-waste collection.

green-glass.label: Green glass
green-glass.tip: Empty and rinse it. Wrap broken pieces in paper and label them so handlers are not hurt.

metal.label: Metal (cans, tins, lids)
metal.tip: Empty and rinse food cans and keep them with the dry recyclables.

paper.label: Paper
paper.tip: Keep it clean and dry. Food-soiled or greasy paper cannot be recycled.

plastic.label: Plastic
plastic.tip: Empty and rinse it, then keep it clean and dry with the other dry recyclables. Never burn plastic.

shoes.label: Shoes / footwear
shoes.tip: If still usable, donate them. Otherwise put them in the dry-waste bin.

trash.label: Non-recyclable item
trash.tip: This cannot be recycled, so it goes in the dry-waste bin. Sanitary items such as diapers or pads belong in the separate sanitary-waste stream.

white-glass.label: Clear glass
white-glass.tip: Empty and rinse it. Wrap broken pieces in paper and label them so handlers are not hurt.
